thread.title_full: Teen's bond hearing reveals mores details Glendale Court killing - NewsBreak

author: Pat Gruner Staff Writer
title: Teen's bond hearing reveals mores details Glendale Court killing - NewsBreak
text: A judge ruled that a teenager remain in custody under a $1 million secured bond after a hearing revealed details about the killing of another teen in a Greenville neighborhood last summer. Jayshawn Barnhill, 17, of 1604 E. Elm St., Goldsboro, was ordered before Special Superior Court Judge Elizabeth Freshwater-Smith on Wednesday in Pitt County Superior Court. The teen remained in restraints during his bond hearing. Barnhill's court-appointed attorney, Jarrette Pittman, told the judge that his client on Sept. 19 was at a home where Keshawn Barrett, 17, was showing a firearm to two other juveniles. Greenville police said the home was in the 600 block of Glen Dale Drive, in the Glendale Court Apartments off of Hooker Road near J.H. Rose High School. Police said that Barrett was located suffering from multiple gunshot wounds after a ShotSpotter alert. He was transported to ECU Health Medical Center where he died a short time later. Police located Barnhill in the area and charged him. His identity was initially kept from the public due to his age at the time of the shooting. He was 16. Police confirmed his identity prior to court proceedings last week. Pittman said that private and city cameras show Barnhill and Barrett get into a scuffle in the yard, at which point Barrett's mother throws open a door and both Barrett and Barnhill run into the residence, where they cannot be seen on camera. He said the ShotSpotter alert registered one gunshot followed by five to six more. He said Barnhill only fired once. Barnhill is currently being held in a Hertford detention center, Pittman said. He requested that his client receive a $100,000 secured bond, which he said would still be difficult for the family to pay, so that he can more easily access Barnhill. Pittman expects that the case will go to trial, not be resolved by a plea deal. The prosecution, led by Pitt County Assistant District Attorney Jordy McCaffity, disputed the defense's account of the facts of the case. McCaffity said that cameras show Barnhill approach Barrett's home and then flee the scene. He said that Barnhill was holding a firearm as he ran from the home and that Barrett, who was already shot, only drew his firearm in pursuit, refuting any claim of Barnhill firing his weapon in self-defense. McCaffity added that both the firearms used in the crime belonged to Barnhill and that the scuffle at the home resulted from his attempt to get the weapon Barrett showed to the other juveniles back from him. He said that the gun used to shoot Barrett was located when detectives backtracked along Barnhill's footpath. Barnhill's bond is already lower than the standard $2 million in Pitt County first-degree murder cases, McCaffity said. The state fears that Barnhill is a flight risk, as he was known to travel from Goldsboro to Greenville. McCaffity said that he was at one point reported missing to Goldsboro police, a claim verified by a post from the police department on social media. He added there are concerns of street gang involvement and possible retribution on Barrett's family and witnesses, as well as danger to the general public since two firearms were involved in the incident. Freshwater-Smith did not take long to decide that Barrett's bond remain at $1 million. She said the purpose of a bond is to ensure someone appears in court and to protect the community. Barnhill's next administrative court hearing is set for Oct. 8. Subscribe to The Daily Reflector
